title: Stop the price watchers from alerting on every restart

blocks.text: The trading desk's alerting service runs one price watcher per rule: "tell me when NRDX goes above 250.00", "tell me when KLMT drops below 40.00". The desk writes its own watchers by extending `PriceWatcher`, builds all of them from its configuration at startup, and starts them once the alert channel is up. Since the market-data feed began handing every new subscriber the last price, each restart during trading hours pages the desk with a burst of alerts like `NRDX at 23175 is above 0`, and some rules don't alert on the opening trade at all.

Fix `src/main/java/practice/PriceWatchers.java`. `start()` is still a `TODO`, and the rest of `PriceWatcher` is yours to change too; keep the public constructors and methods as they are, because the desk's own watchers use them.

When you're done, a watcher hears nothing until it is started; once started it hears the last price at once and every trade after it, and judges each one against its own limit, whichever class defines that limit. About four lines in total.
The tests use a feed that hands the last price to a new subscriber on the subscribing thread, and a watcher of the desk's own that the file doesn't know about.

cases.says: a started watcher, the desk's own or the built-in one, alerts on the trades past its limit and on no others
a watcher started while the last price is inside its limit raises nothing
a watcher started while the last price is already past its limit alerts at once, without waiting for the next trade
a watcher that has been built but not started hears no trade; once started it hears the last one

origin.section: A Constructor That Lets this Escape Hands Out an Object Before It Is Built

concepts: A constructor that hands out this, even on its last line, lets others see a subclass's final fields at their defaults and loses the final-field guarantee; build first, then register or start.
